Lemma
[Smooth Manifold Chart Lemma]

1. ch1:1.35Let $M$ be a set with subsets $U_\alpha $ and maps $\varphi _\alpha :U_\alpha \to \mathbb R^n$ satisfying:

  1. each $\varphi _\alpha $ bijects $U_\alpha $ with an open subset of $\mathbb R^n$;

  2. both $\varphi _\alpha (U_\alpha \cap U_\beta )$ and $\varphi _\beta (U_\alpha \cap U_\beta )$ are open;

  3. on every nonempty overlap, $\varphi _\beta \circ \varphi _\alpha ^{-1}$ is smooth;

  4. a countable subfamily of the $U_\alpha $ covers $M$;

  5. for distinct $p,q\in M$, either some $U_\alpha $ contains both, or there are disjoint $U_\alpha ,U_\beta $ containing $p,q$, respectively.

Then $M$ has a unique smooth manifold structure for which all $(U_\alpha ,\varphi _\alpha )$ are smooth charts.

Proof

\sketch Use the sets $\varphi _\alpha ^{-1}(V)$, with $V\subseteq \mathbb R^n$ open, as a basis. Conditions (ii)–(iii) give

\[ \varphi _\alpha ^{-1}(V)\cap \varphi _\beta ^{-1}(W) =\varphi _\alpha ^{-1}\! \left( V\cap (\varphi _\beta \circ \varphi _\alpha ^{-1})^{-1}(W)\right), \]

so basis intersections are open. Condition (i) makes the resulting space locally Euclidean, (iv) gives second-countability, and (v) gives the Hausdorff property. Condition (iii) then supplies a smooth atlas. The required topology and maximal smooth atlas are forced by the given charts, proving uniqueness.

□
